candidates.title: Prepare a project resume brief

demandEvidence.chore: Keep track of several side projects and remember where work stopped.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I'm usually juggling a few side projects and forgetting where I left off.

ease.reason: A student can test a project-resume summary on supplied sample tasks, but the source documents no summarization or extraction capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent professionals juggling projects might pay to prepare context summaries; the post proves no buyer or willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can turn operator-supplied tasks and notes into a resume brief; integrations and summary accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed run can assemble a brief from supplied notes, but a person must choose current tasks and verify the summary; no loop is documented.

evidence.reason: The author describes juggling side projects and forgetting where work stopped, but gives no frequency, fields, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed a narrow brief assembled from operator-supplied project notes to help resume work. The five provisional ratings average 4.6, below threshold; this Show HN post does not establish repeated demand or implementation capability.

candidates.title: Extract company details from German directories

demandEvidence.chore: Enrich German B2B leads by scraping directories and extracting company Impressum details.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I built an end-to-end n8n pipeline for DACH/German B2B lead enrichment that chains German directory scraping with an automated § 5 DDG Impressum extractor .

ease.reason: A beginner can test extraction on synthetic company pages, but no supplied reference demonstrates scraping or Impressum field extraction.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small B2B consultancies may pay for cleaner lead records; this showcase proves neither unmet demand nor willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can extract a few company fields from synthetic pages; live scraping, coverage and legal review remain unresolved.

autonomy.reason: A proposed batch could extract fields repeatedly, but a person must check source pages and errors; no implementation evidence is attached.

evidence.reason: The post literally describes directory scraping and Impressum extraction, but gives no corroborated demand, frequency or field-level results.

candidates.reason: Assessed a four-week mock that extracts non-personal company fields from operator-supplied synthetic directory pages. The post describes an existing pipeline, not an unmet request; no implementation reference is supplied, and the privacy-sensitive contact fields are excluded. Mean 4.6 is below threshold.

steps.message: Retained the Orbit assessment and the four other evidence-limited exclusions.
